title: Tell terminating from repeating decimals and write repeating decimals with bar notation

lesson.title: Decimals That Stop, Decimals That Keep Going

steps.say: You already know how to turn a fraction into a decimal by dividing the top number by the bottom number. Today we look at what happens after you divide, because some decimals stop and some never do.

Start with one quarter. One divided by four gives zero point two five, and then the division is finished, with nothing left over. A decimal that finishes like this is called terminating, because it lands on an exact spot and stops.

visual.caption: 0.25 lands exactly on one quarter, then stops

steps.say: Now try one third. One divided by three gives zero point three three three, and every time you divide you get another three, forever. It never lands exactly on a spot you can write down with a few digits. That is a repeating decimal.

visual.caption: One third sits between 0.33 and 0.34, never on a neat stopping point

steps.say: Writing threes forever is not practical, so mathematicians use a bar. Put a bar over the digits that repeat, and it means those digits go on and on. Zero point three with a bar over the three means the threes never stop. And two elevenths is zero point one eight one eight one eight, so the bar goes over both the one and the eight.

Here is the mistake I see most often. Somebody writes that one third equals zero point three three, full stop. But zero point three three is only thirty three hundredths, and one third is a tiny bit bigger, sitting just to the right of it. Zero point three three is a rounded-off neighbour, not the real thing. Only the bar tells the truth.

visual.caption: 0.33 stops short; one third is slightly further along

steps.say: So every fraction gives you a decimal that either stops or repeats, and when it repeats you wear the bar with pride.

lesson.answer: If the division stops, the decimal terminates; if the same digits keep coming back, it repeats — and you write it with a bar on top.

practice.question: At the school fundraiser you sold seven of the eight cinnamon buns you baked, and your friend sold four of her nine. Change each fraction to a decimal by dividing the top by the bottom. Which one terminates and which one repeats? Write the repeating one using bar notation.
practice.answer: Seven eighths is zero point eight seven five, which terminates. Four ninths is zero point four four four four and so on, which repeats, so you write it as zero point four with a bar over the four.
